changes.result: Public program, cwd, and artifact paths are relative and descriptor-opened with no-follow semantics. Every .codex-worktree path component is rejected, and the tree witness prunes that directory before traversal.

Actual target execution is intentionally unavailable. A non-preinterrupted request returns a stable causal error before SandboxPlan construction, program or cwd open, tree walk, artifact read, or spawn.

The recorded future plan is deny-default, denies network, fork, process execution, signals, clone, and link operations, and grants file reads only under the parameterized worktree while explicitly denying the prohibited environment path. No shell or system-runtime read allowance remains.

Untyped argv, environment, and artifact builders were removed. Public and secret channels are distinct types; secret sources bind to LiveContext public versions; secret values cannot cross into public fields.

Captured argument and environment records contain source identity and public version only for secret inputs. Secret bytes and their SHA-256 digests are absent from canonical JSON. Secret artifacts reject generically before any path open or read.
Public artifacts are bounded, descriptor-pinned, copied into immutable Arc-backed memory, and exposed without a path-rereading resolver. Mutation after capture cannot change observed bytes.

Specifications bound argv, environment, timeout, retained output, total observed output, artifact count, and aggregate artifact bytes. Because product execution is disabled, output is always empty in product observations; a test-only drain helper proves aggregate overflow detection and child reap behavior.
No root wiring, Cargo dependency, public witness, generated catalog, schema, migration registry, claim registry, state store, package, or release surface was modified.

findings.finding: The six independent rework findings are closed at the no-spawn candidate scope: worktree confinement and prohibited-path canaries, shell exec/source rejection, typed sensitivity channels and secret non-serialization, total resource bounds, immutable artifact observations, and exact WorkerResult-v1 shape.

HCT-CAPTURE does not execute subprocesses. No proven substrate both confines filesystem effects and prevents an allowed shell wrapper from executing or sourcing unpinned secondary code. Every ordinary CommandSpec run therefore rejects before target open or spawn.

WorkspaceWrite, ExternalWrite, and Destructive capture have no descriptor-brokered effect substrate. Setup, retrofit, repair, migration, and other mutating product journeys cannot depend on this candidate.

Aggregate output accounting and overflow cleanup are exercised by a direct test fixture only. They are not production evidence because the production process path is disabled and always emits empty output.
Secret artifact capture is deliberately unsupported and rejects before read. Only explicitly public, bounded artifacts can be captured into immutable memory.
Preinterrupted observations currently require the fixed macOS sandbox-exec capability record. Non-macOS hosts reject even though no target is spawned.
Public integration, old capture authority retirement, generated catalog and schema projection, migration routing, claim decisions, and HCT-CAPTURE acceptance remain root-only.
